status: Experimental repertoire with a generated glyph draft. Fluent Tamil review remains open.

normalisation.aliases: NFD aliases preserve every distinct canonical decomposition. The SA-based shrii alias has a separate equivalence relationship.
normalisation.note: The local Python normalisation database predates Unicode 17. All Tamil decomposition mappings used here are long-established mappings.

sources.role: Assigned Tamil and Tamil Supplement scalars, official names and general categories. ASCII support names.
Checked for additional Tamil sequences. There are none in Unicode 17.0.0.
Section 12.6 documents Tamil rendering, kssa, both shrii spellings, named sequences and historic symbols.

limitations: This inventory proves sequence coverage. It does not prove legible or correct glyph drawings.
A fluent Tamil reader must review the glyph shapes, vowel forms, pulli placement, spacing and shrii ligature.
The inventory uses modern Tamil orthography. Traditional glyph alternates do not receive duplicate Unicode entries.
Historic Tamil Supplement symbols are included for the superset. Most do not belong in normal game UI.
Tamil-script extensions for other languages that require Grantha combining marks, superscript transcription digits or other script blocks are outside this experiment.
Danda and double danda are unified Indic punctuation in the Devanagari block. They are outside this Tamil-block and ASCII inventory.
Join controls, broken combining sequences and arbitrary consonant clusters are outside the glyph inventory. A production renderer must handle or reject them deliberately.
ASCII letters already have existing game artwork. This experiment includes ASCII digits, punctuation and space only.
A repertoire entry represents a Unicode character or a complete text sequence. It is not necessarily one shaped font glyph.
The inventory does not enable a Tamil locale or integrate Tamil shaping into the app.
